saints.name: St. Frances of Rome
saints.title: Religious, Foundress of the Oblates
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman wife and mother who served the poor through plague and war and founded the Oblates of Mary…
biography: Born Francesca Bussa de' Leoni at Rome in 1384, Frances longed for the cloister but was married at about twelve to Lorenzo Ponziani, commander of papal troops. The arranged marriage proved happy and lasted forty years; with her sister-in-law Vannozza she made the palace a dispensary for the poor.

Through the wars of the Western Schism, plague that carried off two children, and famine, she opened her home as a hospital and drove her own wagon to gather wood and herbs. When Lorenzo returned ruined and wounded, she nursed him to the end.

In 1425 she gathered devout Roman women into the Oblates of Mary, bound by no vows and living in their own homes under the Benedictines of Santa Maria Nova; in 1433 she founded for them the monastery of Tor de' Specchi, approved by Pope Eugene IV. After his death in 1436 she joined the community as superior.

She died on 9 March 1440 and was canonized by Pope Paul V in 1608. Because her guardian angel was said to light her way with a lamp when she traveled at night, Pope Pius XI declared her patron of motorists in 1925; she is honored as patron of widows.
saints.knownFor: Uniting family life with heroic charity, and founding the Oblates of Mary.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 9 March
